name: Diazepam
description: Diazepam (Valium) facts: uses for anxiety, alcohol withdrawal, spasms and seizures, risks, interactions, overdose, withdrawal, and legal access.
quick: Diazepam (Valium) is a long-acting benzodiazepine used for anxiety, alcohol withdrawal, muscle spasms, and seizures. Its long half-life makes it a common choice for tapering people off shorter-acting benzodiazepines. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance.
facts: Anxiety, acute alcohol withdrawal, muscle spasm, seizure clusters (adjunct)
Tablets, oral solution, nasal spray, rectal gel, injection
Up to 48 hours; active metabolite up to 100 hours
Use with opioids; misuse and addiction; dependence and withdrawal

profile.duration: Effects can last a day or more

blocks.p: Diazepam is approved for anxiety disorders, short-term relief of anxiety symptoms, acute alcohol withdrawal, as an add-on for skeletal muscle spasm, and as an add-on for convulsive disorders. The nasal spray and rectal gel treat seizure clusters outside the hospital.[[1]]

Diazepam and its active metabolite, desmethyldiazepam, stay in the body for days. This smooths out blood levels, which is why clinicians often switch patients to diazepam before a slow benzodiazepine taper.

The figures below come from the FDA-approved label and describe how prescribers typically use diazepam. They are not personal dosing advice. A prescriber sets the dose for each person and adjusts it over time.[[1]]

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of diazepam?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warnings
items: Taking benzodiazepines with opioids can cause profound sedation, slowed breathing, coma, and death.[[2]]
Benzodiazepines can be misused and can lead to addiction, which raises the risk of overdose and death.[[3]]
Regular use can cause physical dependence. Stopping suddenly or cutting the dose quickly can cause withdrawal reactions, including seizures, that can be life-threatening.[[3]]

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include drowsiness, fatigue, muscle weakness, and poor coordination.[[1]]

**Accumulation:** because diazepam builds up over days, sedation can increase over the first week, especially in older adults and people with liver disease. It is on the Beers list of medicines older adults should usually avoid.

sections.q: What does diazepam overdose look like?

blocks.p: Diazepam overdose causes deep sleepiness, confusion, slurred speech, poor coordination, and, with opioids or alcohol, slowed or stopped breathing.[[1]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, hard to wake, or breathing slowly.
For advice when the person is awake and stable, call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 (US, free, 24 hours).
If opioids could be involved, including pills not from a pharmacy, give naloxone if you have it. Naloxone does not reverse diazepam, but it will not harm the person.
Stay with the person and place them on their side if they are drowsy or vomiting.

sections.q: What is diazepam withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

blocks.p: People who take diazepam regularly, even as prescribed, can become physically dependent within weeks. Because diazepam lasts so long, withdrawal starts later, often several days after the last dose, and tends to be gentler at onset.[[3]]

timeline.title: Symptoms begin
timeline.text: Rebound anxiety, insomnia, restlessness, sweating, and tremor.

timeline.title: Acute withdrawal
timeline.text: Panic, irritability, muscle pain, nausea, sensitivity to light and sound, and in severe cases seizures or delirium.

timeline.title: Protracted symptoms in some people
timeline.text: A minority have lingering anxiety, poor sleep, low mood, or tingling that can last weeks to more than 12 months.

blocks.warn: Stopping diazepam abruptly after regular use can cause seizures. The dose should be reduced gradually under the care of a prescriber.

blocks.p: Because of its long half-life, diazepam is often used as the drug of choice for tapering. Reductions of 5 to 10% every 2 to 4 weeks are common, adjusted to symptoms.[[4]]

sections.q: How do you get diazepam legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, diazepam is a Schedule IV controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[5]]

ul: **Refills:** a Schedule IV prescription can be refilled up to five times within six months of the date it was written. After that, a new prescription is needed.[[6]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[7]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[8]][[9]]

blocks.warn: Pills sold as Valium outside a pharmacy are often counterfeit. The DEA reports that fake pills frequently contain fentanyl or methamphetamine, and they cannot be told apart by appearance.[[10]]

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill diazepam prescriptions online and ship them. Buying diazepam from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[8]][[10]]

steps: A clinician evaluates you in person or by telemedicine and decides whether diazepam is appropriate.
The prescription goes to a pharmacy
Prescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
The pharmacy checks and fills it
A pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells diazepam with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[8]][[9]]

faq: How long does diazepam stay in your system?
Diazepam and its active metabolite can remain for several days to more than a week. Urine tests can detect it for up to 10 days, and longer after heavy use.
Per milligram, alprazolam is about 10 to 20 times as potent, but diazepam lasts much longer. 10 mg of diazepam is roughly equivalent to 0.5 to 1 mg of alprazolam.
Why is diazepam used for alcohol withdrawal?
It calms the overactive brain state of withdrawal, prevents seizures, and lasts long enough to provide a smooth, self-tapering effect.
Can diazepam be used for muscle spasms?
Yes, as an add-on for spasm from injury or conditions such as cerebral palsy.
